Furthermore, the company achieves a tangible book value of ₹ 153 against its share price of ₹ 400 [E1], anchoring the equity in solid net asset backing. This extreme pricing sits on top of a structurally decaying top-line, demonstrated by compounded sales growth contracting across every measurable horizon: -3% over 10 years, -15% over 5 years, -19% over 3 years, and plunging by -40% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14, E15, E16]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has collapsed by -107% [E18], confirming that the operational engine is moving backward despite rich market pricing. Compounding these fundamental deterioration signals, the return on equity sits at 0% compared to a sector benchmark of 4.93% [E8], and return on assets is negative at -1.11% against a sector benchmark of 1.8% [E7]. Furthermore, the business offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3] and has been flagged for poor five-year sales growth [E52], while expectations measured by recent price growth exceed profit growth by 100% [E47]. The bear points to the high price-to-earnings ratio [E5], but this overlooks the reality of accelerating earnings growth and a screening reason showing profit growth exceeding 20% year-over-year [E57]. Furthermore, the bear flags negative return on assets [E7], yet the company trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 2.61x relative to a book value of ₹ 153 [E1], which is comparable to the sector benchmark price-to-book of 2.55x [E6]. The bull leans on accelerating earnings growth and a screen for profit growth exceeding 20% year-over-year [E57, E59], but this ignores the catastrophic collapse in trailing twelve-month profit growth of -107% [E18] that completely undermines any near-term momentum argument. While the bull downplays poor historical sales by citing sector tailwinds of 16.5% median sales growth and 25.0% median profit growth [E64, E65], the company's own compounded sales growth metrics are aggressively moving in the exact opposite direction—contracting by 3% over 10 years, 15% over 5 years, 19% over 3 years, and a staggering 40% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14, E15, E16, E52].
